title.zh: 卷249 列傳三十六 索尼 苏克萨哈 遏必隆 鳌拜
title.en: Volume 249 Biographies 36: Suo Ni, Su Kesaha, E Bi Long, Ao Bai
title.raw: 卷249 列傳三十六 索尼 苏克萨哈 遏必隆 鳌拜

sentences.zh: 索尼，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黄旗人。

translations.literal: Sonin, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin belonged to the Heseri clan and came from the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父碩色，大學士希福兄也，太祖時，自哈達挈家來歸。

translations.literal: His father Shuose was the elder brother of Grand Secretary Xifu; in the Taizu era he brought his household from Hada to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuose was elder brother to Grand Secretary Xifu; during Taizu’s reign the family left Hada and came over to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其兄弟父子並通國書及蒙、漢文字，命碩色與希福同直文館，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: Because the father and sons of the brothers alike were versed in the national script and in Mongol and Chinese writing, the Taizu ordered Shuose and Xifu to serve together in the Literary Institute and bestowed on them the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: Since both brothers and their sons mastered the national script as well as Mongol and Chinese, Taizu had Shuose and Xifu attend the Literary Institute together and granted them the title "Bakshi."

sentences.zh: 授索尼一等侍衛。

translations.literal: Sonin was appointed a first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a first-class imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 從征界籓、棟夔。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against Jiefan and Dongkui.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field in expeditions to Jiefan and Dongkui.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從太宗攻錦州，偵敵甯遠，並有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed the Taizong in the attack on Jinzhou, reconnoitered the enemy at Ningyuan, and won merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong year one he followed Emperor Taizong against Jinzhou, scouted the foe at Ningyuan, and distinguished himself in each action.

sentences.zh: 二年，上親征喀爾喀，徵兵外籓，科爾沁不至。

translations.literal: In the second year the emperor personally campaigned against the Khalkha; when troops were levied from the outer banners, the Khorchin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In year two the throne led a personal expedition against the Khalkha; levies from the outer banners were called, but the Khorchin failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 命索尼與侍衛阿珠祜齎諭飭責土謝圖額駙奥巴。

translations.literal: Sonin was ordered, together with guardsman Azhuhu, to carry edicts rebuking Tuxie Tu taiji Oba.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Sonin and guardsman Azhuhu with imperial instructions to reprimand Tuxie Tu taiji Oba.

sentences.zh: 初，奥巴爲台吉，入朝，太祖以貝勒舒爾哈齊女妻焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Oba was still a taiji, he came to court and Taizu gave him in marriage a daughter of Prince Shuerhaqi.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, while Oba was still a taiji, he visited court and Taizu married him to a daughter of Prince Shuerhaqi.

sentences.zh: 既而奥巴屢背約，私與明通，復徵兵不至。

translations.literal: Later Oba repeatedly broke his pledges, dealt secretly with the Ming, and again failed to send troops when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Oba broke faith again and again, trafficked privately with the Ming, and once more ignored the call for troops.

sentences.zh: 索尼受方略行，既入境，其部人饋以牲，索尼不受，曰：「爾汗有異心，爾物豈可食耶？」

translations.literal: Sonin carried out the strategy he had been given; once inside Oba’s territory, the tribesmen offered him livestock, which Sonin refused, saying, "Your khan harbors disloyal intent—how could I eat your food?"
translations.idiomatic: Sonin executed the plan entrusted to him; on entering the territory, tribesmen offered livestock, but he refused, saying, "Your khan is disloyal—how could I accept your food?"

sentences.zh: 時奥巴病足，索尼與阿珠祜見公主，以諭旨告。

translations.literal: At that time Oba’s feet were afflicted; Sonin and Azhuhu saw the princess and delivered the imperial message.
translations.idiomatic: Oba’s feet were then diseased; Sonin and Azhuhu saw the princess and conveyed the edict.

sentences.zh: 奥巴聞之，扶掖至，佯問曰：「此爲誰？」

translations.literal: When Oba heard this he had himself supported forward and feigned to ask, "Who are these men?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Oba had himself helped forward and pretended to ask, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 索尼曰：「吾儕天使也！

translations.literal: Sonin said, "We are envoys of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Sonin replied, "We are the emperor’s envoys!

sentences.zh: 爾有罪，義當絕。

translations.literal: You are guilty and ought to be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: You stand guilty and deserve extinction.

sentences.zh: 今特以公主故，使來餽問耳。」

translations.literal: Now we come only because of the princess, to bring greetings and inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: We come now solely for the princess’s sake, to bring inquiries."

sentences.zh: 奥巴顧左右趣具饌，索尼等不顧而出。

translations.literal: Oba looked to his attendants to hurry a feast, but Sonin and the others left without a glance.
translations.idiomatic: Oba signaled his attendants to prepare a banquet, but Sonin and his party departed without looking back.

sentences.zh: 奥巴恐，使台吉塞冷等請其事。

translations.literal: Oba grew afraid and sent taiji Saileng and others to ask what was intended.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the consequences, Oba sent taiji Saileng and others to learn their purpose.

sentences.zh: 索尼出璽書示之，即令從者先行。

translations.literal: Sonin produced the imperial seal-document and showed it, then ordered the attendants to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin displayed the sealed imperial letter and ordered his followers to proceed first.

sentences.zh: 奥巴得書大驚，令所屬大臣跽留，索尼責以大義，奥巴叩首悔罪，願入朝。

translations.literal: Oba, greatly alarmed on receiving the document, had his ministers kneel and detain them; Sonin rebuked him on principle, Oba kowtowed in repentance and vowed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the document, Oba was terrified and had his ministers kneel to detain the envoys; Sonin upbraided him on moral grounds until Oba kowtowed in remorse and pledged to attend court.

sentences.zh: 索尼與阿珠祜偕其大臣黨阿賴先歸奏狀，帝甚悦。

translations.literal: Sonin and Azhuhu returned ahead with his minister Dangalai to report; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin and Azhuhu came back first with minister Dangalai to present their report, and the emperor was highly pleased.

sentences.zh: 三年，從大軍入關，薄燕京，明督師袁崇煥赴援，列營城東南。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the main army through the passes, approached Yanjing, and when Ming Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan came to relieve the city he drew up camps southeast of it.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he marched with the main force through the frontier, drew near Beijing, and when Ming commander Yuan Chonghuan hurried to the relief he pitched camps southeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 貝勒豪格突入陣，敵兵蹙之，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: Prince Hooge charged into the enemy formation; the foe pressed in on him and arrows and stones fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hooge broke into the enemy line; troops closed around him while arrows and stones poured down.

sentences.zh: 索尼躍馬馳入，斬殺甚眾，拔豪格破圍出。

translations.literal: Sonin spurred his horse in, killed many in the press, and broke the encirclement to bring Hooge out.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin galloped in, slew a great number, and cut a path to rescue Hooge from the siege.

sentences.zh: 四年，諭降榛子鎮、沙河驛，拔永平，守之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took part in reducing Zhenzi Town and Shahe Post and capturing Yongping, which he then garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he helped reduce Zhenzi Town and Shahe Courier Station, seized Yongping, and held it.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢吏部啟心郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Qixinlang of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he rose to Qixinlang in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 從圍大凌河。

translations.literal: He joined the siege of Dalinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in besieging Dalinghe.

sentences.zh: 明兵自錦州來援，敗之。

translations.literal: When Ming troops came from Jinzhou to relieve the place, they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces marching from Jinzhou to relieve the fortress were beaten off.

sentences.zh: 六年，從征察哈爾，略大同，取阜臺台寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he campaigned against the Chahar, raided Datong, and took the Fotai platform stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he joined the expedition against the Chahar, raided Datong, and captured the Fotai platform fort.

sentences.zh: 尋予牛錄章京世職，仍直内院。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the hereditary office of niru captain and continued to attend the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the hereditary post of niru captain while still serving in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 崇德八年，考績，進三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongde, on the merit review, he was advanced to third-rank ala captain.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde year eight, at the performance review, he was promoted to third-rank ala captain.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩后五日，睿親王多爾衮詣三官廟，召索尼議册立。

translations.literal: Five days after the Taizong’s death, Prince Rui Dorgon went to the Sanguan Shrine and summoned Sonin to discuss enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Five days after Taizong died, Prince Rui Dorgon came to the Sanguan Shrine and called Sonin to counsel on the succession.

sentences.zh: 索尼曰：「先帝有皇子在，必立其一。

translations.literal: Sonin said, "The late emperor left imperial sons—one of them must be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin said, "The late emperor has sons—one of them must be raised to the throne.

sentences.zh: 他非所知也。」

translations.literal: I know nothing beyond that."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that I know nothing."

sentences.zh: 是夕，巴牙喇纛章京圖賴詣索尼，告以定立皇子。

translations.literal: That night Baturu banner captain Tulai came to Sonin and told him the decision to enthrone a prince.
translations.idiomatic: That night Baturu banner captain Tulai visited Sonin and announced that a prince had been chosen.

sentences.zh: 黎明，兩黄旗大臣盟於大清門，令兩旗巴牙喇兵張弓挾矢，環立宫殿，率以詣崇政殿。

translations.literal: At dawn the ministers of the two Yellow Banners swore alliance at the Daqing Gate, ordered Baturu troops of both banners to string bows and hold arrows, and ringed the palace; they led them to the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak ministers of the two Yellow Banners swore alliance at the Daqing Gate, drew up Baturu archers of both banners around the palace, and marched them to Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣列坐東西廡，索尼及巴圖魯鄂拜首言立皇子，睿親王令暫退。

translations.literal: Princes and ministers sat in the east and west corridors; Sonin and the warrior Ebai were first to speak for enthroning a prince, and Prince Rui ordered a recess.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers took seats in the east and west wings; Sonin and warrior Ebai were first to urge enthroning a prince, whereupon Prince Rui called a pause.

sentences.zh: 英親王阿濟格、豫親王多鐸勸睿親王即帝位，睿親王猶豫未允，豫親王曰：「若不允，當立我。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Ajige and Prince Yu Dodo urged Prince Rui to take the throne himself; Prince Rui hesitated and would not consent, and Prince Yu said, "If you refuse, then enthrone me—I am named in Taizu’s testament.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Ajige and Prince Yu Dodo pressed Prince Rui to become emperor; he still hesitated, and Prince Yu said, "If you will not, then set me on the throne—my name stands in Taizu’s will.

sentences.zh: 我名在太祖遺詔。」

translations.literal: I am named in Taizu’s testament."
translations.idiomatic: My name stands in Taizu’s will."

sentences.zh: 睿親王曰：「肅親王亦有名，不獨王也。」

translations.literal: Prince Rui said, "Prince Su is also named—not you alone."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui replied, "Prince Su is named as well—not you alone."

sentences.zh: 豫親王又曰：「不立我，論長當立禮親王。」

translations.literal: Prince Yu said again, "If not me, then by seniority it should be the Prince of Rites."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu added, "If not me, then by precedence it should be the Prince of Rites."

sentences.zh: 禮親王曰：「睿親王若允，我國之福。

translations.literal: The Prince of Rites said, "If Prince Rui consents, it is our dynasty’s good fortune;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rites said, "If Prince Rui accepts, it is the fortune of the state;

sentences.zh: 否則當立皇子。

translations.literal: otherwise a prince must be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: if not, a prince must reign.

sentences.zh: 我老矣，能勝此耶？」

translations.literal: I am old; could I bear this burden?"
translations.idiomatic: I am aged; how could I sustain such a weight?"

sentences.zh: 乃定議奉世祖即位。

translations.literal: Thus the decision was fixed to install the Shizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly then resolved to enthrone the Shizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 索尼與譚泰、圖賴、鞏阿岱、錫翰、鄂拜盟於三官廟，誓輔幼主，六人如一體。

translations.literal: Sonin, with Tan Tai, Tulai, Gongadai, Xi Han, and Ebai, swore alliance at the Sanguan Shrine to assist the young lord—the six as one body.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin joined Tan Tai, Tulai, Gongadai, Xi Han, and Ebai in oath at the Sanguan Shrine to aid the young sovereign, the six united as one.

sentences.zh: 都統何洛會等訐告肅親王豪格，王坐廢，詔褒索尼不附王，賜鞍馬。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief He Luohui and others denounced Prince Su Hooge; the prince was deposed, and an edict praised Sonin for not siding with the prince and granted him saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief He Luohui impeached Prince Su Hooge; the prince was removed, and an edict commended Sonin for refusing to follow him, bestowing saddle and horse.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從睿親王入關，定京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Rui through the passes and settled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year one he followed Prince Rui into China and established the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年，晉二等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to second-rank angbang captain.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was raised to second-rank angbang captain.

sentences.zh: 睿親王令解啟心郎職，仍理部事。

translations.literal: Prince Rui ordered him relieved of the Qixinlang post while he still handled board affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui removed him from Qixinlang but left him in charge of ministry business.

sentences.zh: 睿親王方擅政，譚泰、鞏阿岱、錫翰皆背盟附之，憾索尼不附。

translations.literal: Prince Rui was then monopolizing power; Tan Tai, Gongadai, and Xi Han all broke the alliance to join him and resented Sonin’s refusal.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Rui held arbitrary power, Tan Tai, Gongadai, and Xi Han broke their oaths to side with him and bore Sonin a grudge for standing apart.

sentences.zh: 李自成之敗也，焚宫殿西走。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng was defeated he burned the palaces and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng’s defeat sent him burning the palaces as he fled westward.

sentences.zh: 至是議修建，睿親王亦營第，勼工庀材，工部給直偏厚，諸匠役皆急營王第。

translations.literal: Plans were now made to rebuild; Prince Rui also built a mansion, mustering craftsmen and stockpiling materials—the Works Ministry paid rates far on the generous side, and every artisan hurried the prince’s house.
translations.idiomatic: Reconstruction was debated; Prince Rui raised his own residence too, crowding workers and materials—the Board of Works paid lavish rates and all labor rushed the prince’s mansion.

sentences.zh: 佟機言於王，王怒，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Tong Ji spoke to the prince; the prince grew angry and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Ji remonstrated with the prince, who in rage meant to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 索尼力言其無罪，王以是愈憾索尼。

translations.literal: Sonin strongly argued his innocence, and the prince’s resentment toward Sonin deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin insisted on his innocence, which only deepened the prince’s dislike of Sonin.

sentences.zh: 英親王阿濟格慢上，目爲「八歲幼兒」，索尼以告睿親王，請罪之，王不許。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Ajige showed disrespect to the throne, calling the emperor an "eight-year child"; Sonin reported this to Prince Rui and asked punishment, but the prince would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Ajige slighted the sovereign, calling him an "eight-year child"; Sonin told Prince Rui and sought penalties, but the prince refused.

sentences.zh: 王嘗召諸大臣議分封諸王，索尼持不可。

translations.literal: When the prince once summoned ministers to discuss enfeoffing princes, Sonin held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the prince gathered ministers to parcel domains among princes; Sonin objected.

sentences.zh: 鞏阿岱、錫翰進曰：「索尼不欲王平天下乎？」

translations.literal: Gongadai and Xi Han advanced and said, "Does Sonin not wish the prince to pacify the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongadai and Xi Han stepped forward saying, "Does Sonin not want the prince to bring the empire to peace?"

sentences.zh: 請罪之，王亦不許。

translations.literal: They asked that he be punished, but the prince again would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded his punishment, yet the prince again declined.

sentences.zh: 索尼發固山額真譚泰隱匿詔旨，譚泰坐削公爵；

translations.literal: Sonin exposed gusa ejen Tan Tai for concealing an edict; Tan Tai was reduced from duke for it;
translations.idiomatic: Sonin denounced gusa ejen Tan Tai for hiding an edict, and Tan Tai was stripped of his dukedom;

sentences.zh: 因訐索尼以内庫漆琴與人，及使牧者秣馬庫院，傔從捕魚禁門橋下，索尼遂坐罷。

translations.literal: they then accused Sonin of giving a lacquered zither from the inner store to another and of having herdsmen fodder horses in the treasury yard and retainers fish beneath the Forbidden Gate bridge—Sonin was dismissed for these charges.
translations.idiomatic: they then impeached Sonin for giving a lacquered qin from the inner treasury to another, for pasturing horses in the storehouse court, and for retainers fishing under the palace bridge—on these grounds Sonin was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 三年，巴牙喇纛章京圖賴劾譚泰怨望，詞涉索尼。

translations.literal: In the third year Baturu banner captain Tulai impeached Tan Tai for disaffection, with words touching Sonin.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Baturu banner captain Tulai charged Tan Tai with resentment, implicating Sonin in the wording.

sentences.zh: 順治初，大軍分道剿賊西安，譚泰後至，無功。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi the main armies divided to suppress rebels at Xi’an; Tan Tai arrived late and won no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi the armies split to crush rebels at Xi’an; Tan Tai came late and gained no credit.

sentences.zh: 及移師江南，譚泰慮勿預，語圖賴，甚怏怏。

translations.literal: When the force shifted to the south, Tan Tai feared being left out, spoke with Tulai, and was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: On the move to the south Tan Tai feared exclusion, spoke with Tulai, and grew very bitter.

sentences.zh: 圖賴遺書索尼，使啟睿親王，齎書者私發之，恐譚泰獲罪，沉諸河。

translations.literal: Tulai sent a letter to Sonin to lay the matter before Prince Rui; the bearer opened it privately, fearing Tan Tai would be condemned, and sank it in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Tulai wrote Sonin to raise the matter with Prince Rui; the courier opened it on his own, dreading Tan Tai’s ruin, and threw the letter into the river.

sentences.zh: 圖賴發前事，逮訊齎書者塞爾特，詭云書巳達索尼。

translations.literal: Tulai brought out the earlier affair and seized the courier Sailte for examination; he falsely said the letter had already reached Sonin.
translations.idiomatic: Tulai revived the affair and arrested the courier Sailte, who falsely claimed the letter had reached Sonin.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣論索尼罪當斬，王親鞫之，索尼曰：「吾前發譚泰匿詔旨罪，顧匿圖賴書以庇之乎？」

translations.literal: The ministers judged Sonin deserving of death; the prince personally tried him, and Sonin said, "I earlier exposed Tan Tai for hiding an edict—would I now hide Tulai’s letter to shield him?"
translations.idiomatic: Ministers ruled Sonin should die; the prince interrogated him in person, and Sonin said, "I once denounced Tan Tai for concealing an edict—would I hide Tulai’s letter to protect him?"

sentences.zh: 王窮訊齎書者，事得白。

translations.literal: The prince pressed the courier in questioning and the truth came out.
translations.idiomatic: The prince examined the courier closely and the facts were cleared.

sentences.zh: 尋復世職，然王與譚泰等憾索尼滋甚。

translations.literal: Soon Sonin’s hereditary office was restored, yet the prince and Tan Tai and the rest hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His hereditary post was soon restored, but the prince, Tan Tai, and the others resented him still more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 五年，值清明，遣索尼祭昭陵，既行，貝子屯齊訐索尼與圖賴等謀立肅親王，論死，末減，奪官，籍其家，即安置昭陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, at the Qingming festival, Sonin was sent to sacrifice at Zhaoling; he had already set out when Prince Tunqi denounced Sonin and Tulai and others for plotting to enthrone Prince Su—death was decreed, reduced at the end, offices taken, household registered, and he was stationed at once at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, on Qingming, Sonin was dispatched to offer sacrifice at Zhaoling; after he had departed, Prince Tunqi accused Sonin, Tulai, and others of scheming to raise Prince Su—the sentence was death, commuted in the end to loss of rank, confiscation of property, and immediate assignment at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，特召還，復世職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Shizu Emperor took power in person and specially recalled him, restoring his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, when the Shunzhi Emperor assumed personal rule, Sonin was specially recalled and his hereditary post restored.

sentences.zh: 累進一等伯世襲，擢内大臣，兼議政大臣、總管内務府。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to first-rank baron with hereditary succession, raised to inner minister, and concurrently made deliberating minister and superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to first-rank baron with hereditary succession, became inner minister, and also served as deliberating minister and superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 十七年，應詔上言，略謂：「小民冤抑，有司不爲詳審者，請嚴察，使毋壅於上聞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, responding to an imperial call for memorials, he wrote in summary: "When common people suffer injustice and officials do not investigate thoroughly, please enforce strict scrutiny so nothing is blocked from reaching the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, answering the throne’s invitation to memorialize, he wrote in part: "When humble subjects are wronged and officials fail to examine the case fully, strict oversight is needed so complaints are not stopped before they reach Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 犯罪發覺，其奉有嚴旨者，有司輙從重比，不無枉濫。

translations.literal: When crimes are discovered and stern edicts have been issued, officials tend to apply the heavier analogy and wrongful executions are not absent—please order the judiciary to weigh cases with care.
translations.idiomatic: When offenses come to light under stern edicts, magistrates often apply the harsher statute, and innocent men are not spared—command the law officers to judge with caution.

sentences.zh: 請敕法司詳慎。

translations.literal: Please order correction.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court revise this.

sentences.zh: 前議福建將士失律罪，在大將軍止削一不世襲之拜他喇布勒哈番，而所屬將領乃盡奪世職，輕重不平，有乖懲勸，請敕更正。

translations.literal: The earlier deliberation on Fujian officers who broke discipline reduced the grand commander by only one non-hereditary baturu-bule banner rank while subordinate generals lost all hereditary offices—light and heavy punishments were unequal, contrary to discipline and encouragement; please order amendment.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Fujian case the commander-in-chief lost only one non-hereditary baturu-bule banner rank while his subordinates forfeited every hereditary post—the imbalance defeats both justice and incentive; amend the ruling.

sentences.zh: 开國諸臣，自拜他喇布勒哈番以上皆有功業，宜予世襲；

translations.literal: Founding ministers from baturu-bule banner rank upward all earned merit and ought to receive hereditary patents;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who helped found the dynasty, from baturu-bule rank upward, earned their honors and should hold hereditary patents;

sentences.zh: 其后恩詔所加，非有戰功，請毋給世襲敕書。

translations.literal: those later added by grace edicts without battlefield merit should not be given hereditary sealed patents.
translations.idiomatic: later grants under grace edicts without battle service should not carry hereditary sealed patents.

sentences.zh: 在外諸籓，風俗不齊，若必嚴以内定之例，恐反滋擾，請予以優容。

translations.literal: Outer banners differ in custom; if inner regulations are enforced rigidly, disturbance may only increase—please allow leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Outer banners follow unlike customs; rigid enforcement of metropolitan rules may breed unrest—grant them forbearance.

sentences.zh: 大臣奪據行市，奸宄之徒，投托指引，以攘貨財，四方商賈，負擔來京，輙復勒價强買。

translations.literal: Ministers who seize market streets and wicked men who attach themselves to guide trade and seize goods—merchants from every quarter who bear loads to the capital are again forced to sell at dictated prices.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who monopolize market streets, with rogues in their pay to intercept goods, and traders from afar who reach the capital only to be compelled to sell at fixed prices.

sentences.zh: 諸王貝勒及大臣私引玉泉山水灌溉，泉流爲之竭。

translations.literal: Princes, beile, and ministers who privately divert Jade Spring Hill water for irrigation have exhausted the springs.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, beile, and ministers who tap Jade Spring Hill for private irrigation have drained the springs.

sentences.zh: 邊外木植，皆商人雇民采伐。

translations.literal: Timber beyond the frontier is all cut by merchants who hire laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier timber was felled entirely by merchants who hired workers.

sentences.zh: 今又爲大臣私行强占，致商不聊生。

translations.literal: Now ministers seize it by force in private, so that merchants cannot make a living.
translations.idiomatic: Now ministers seize it by force for themselves, leaving merchants destitute.

sentences.zh: 大臣不殫心公事，惟飾宅第。

translations.literal: Ministers do not devote themselves to public business but only adorn their mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers neglect public duty and spend themselves only on embellishing their houses.

sentences.zh: 皆請申禁。

translations.literal: All these he asked be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On all these points he sought strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 五城審事官，遇世族富家與窮民訟者，必罪窮民，曲意徇私，不思執法。

translations.literal: The Five-District judicial officers, when great families sue the poor, always punish the poor and twist the law to favor the powerful, forgetting impartial enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: When wealthy clans sue the poor, Five-District magistrates condemn the poor and bend the law for patrons, forgetting impartial enforcement.

sentences.zh: 請嚴飭毋得枉屈賄庇。」

translations.literal: Please strictly admonish them not to wrong the innocent or take bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Order them sternly not to pervert justice or accept bribes."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上以所奏皆實，飭議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered the throne, finding every point true, ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the emperor, who found each charge true and ordered discussion and enforcement.

sentences.zh: 十八年，世祖崩，遺詔以索尼與蘇克薩哈、遏必隆、鼇拜同輔政。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Shizu Emperor died; the testament named Sonin, Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen the Shunzhi Emperor died; his will named Sonin, Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi as regents.

sentences.zh: 索尼聞命，跪告諸王貝勒，請共任國政，諸王貝勒皆曰：「大行皇帝深知汝四大臣，委以國家重務，誰敢干預？」

translations.literal: On receiving the command Sonin knelt and told the princes and beile, asking them to share state affairs; the princes and beile all said, "The late emperor knew well that you four great ministers were no mediocrities and entrusted you with the weight of the realm—who would dare interfere?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the order, Sonin knelt before the princes and beile and asked them to share governance; they replied, "The late emperor knew you four were no ordinary men and laid the state upon you—who would dare meddle?"

sentences.zh: 索尼等乃奏知皇太后，誓於上帝及大行皇帝前，其辭曰：「先皇帝不以索尼、蘇克薩哈、遏必隆、鼇拜等爲庸劣，遺詔寄託，保翊沖主。

translations.literal: Sonin and the others then reported to the empress dowager and swore before Heaven and the late emperor, their words being: "The late emperor did not regard Sonin, Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi as incompetent and by testament entrusted us to guard and support the young sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: They then informed the empress dowager and swore before Heaven and the late emperor: "The late emperor did not count Sonin, Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi worthless, but by his will charged us to protect the young lord.

sentences.zh: 索尼等誓協忠誠，共生死，輔佐政務。

translations.literal: Sonin and the others vowed loyal unity in life and death and to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: They vowed loyal fellowship in life and death and joint conduct of affairs.

sentences.zh: 不私親戚，不計怨仇，不聽旁人及兄弟子姪教唆之言，不求無義之富貴，不私往來諸王貝勒等府受其餽遺，不結黨羽，不受賄賂，惟以忠心仰報先皇帝大恩。

translations.literal: They would not favor kin, reckon old grudges, heed instigation from outsiders or from brothers and nephews, seek unearned wealth, visit princes and beile in private to accept gifts, form factions, or take bribes—they would repay the late emperor’s great grace only with loyal hearts.
translations.idiomatic: They would not favor relatives, nurse feuds, listen to outsiders or kin who urged private ends, pursue unearned riches, call privately on princes and beile for gifts, form cliques, or take bribes—only loyal hearts to answer the late emperor’s grace.

sentences.zh: 若各爲身謀，有違斯誓，上天殛罰，奪算凶誅。」

translations.literal: If any sought his private interest and broke this oath, Heaven would strike him down, shorten his years, and bring violent death."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever schemed for himself and broke this oath—may Heaven destroy him, cut short his life, and visit sudden ruin."

sentences.zh: 誓訖，乃受事。

translations.literal: When the oath was finished they undertook their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The oath ended and they took up office.

sentences.zh: 世祖定中國，既親政，紀綱法度，循太祖、太宗遺制；

translations.literal: After the Shizu Emperor had settled China and taken personal rule, statutes and measures followed the legacy of Taizu and Taizong;
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shunzhi Emperor had pacified China and ruled in person, law and institution followed Taizu and Taizong;

sentences.zh: 亦頗取明舊典捐益之，務使稱國體。

translations.literal: Ming precedents were also drawn on and trimmed so that they suited the national form.
translations.idiomatic: Ming practice was borrowed and adjusted where it fit the state’s dignity.

sentences.zh: 四輔臣爲政，稱旨諭諸王、貝勒、諸大臣，詳考太祖、太宗成憲，勒爲典章。

translations.literal: When the four regents governed, an edict pleasing to the throne was sent to princes, beile, and ministers to examine carefully the completed statutes of Taizu and Taizong and compile them into canon.
translations.idiomatic: Under the four regents an edict went to princes, beile, and ministers to study Taizu and Taizong’s established institutions and codify them.

sentences.zh: 引世祖遺詔，謂：「不能仰法太祖、太宗，多所更張；

translations.literal: Citing the late emperor’s testament, they said: "We could not follow Taizu and Taizong in many changes;
translations.idiomatic: They quoted the late emperor’s words: "We failed to uphold Taizu and Taizong and changed too much;

sentences.zh: 今當率祖制，復舊章，以副先帝遺意。」

translations.literal: now we should lead by ancestral institutions, restore old regulations, and fulfill the late emperor’s intent."
translations.idiomatic: now we must take ancestral rule as our guide, restore former statutes, and honor the late emperor’s wish."

sentences.zh: 乃改内阁翰林院還爲内三院，復设理籓院，罷裁太常、光禄、鸿胪諸寺。

translations.literal: They then changed the Grand Secretariat and Hanlin Academy back into the Three Inner Courts, re-established the Court of Colonial Affairs, and abolished the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of State Ceremonial, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: They restored the Inner Three Courts in place of the Grand Secretariat and Hanlin Academy, re-founded the Court of Colonial Affairs, and abolished the Courts of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, and State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 他舉措皆类是。

translations.literal: Other measures were all of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: Their other actions followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 而鑲黄、正白兩旗互易圈地，兴大獄。

translations.literal: The Bordered Yellow and Plain White banners exchanged estate lands, and a great case arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Bordered Yellow and Plain White banners swapped allotted estates, provoking a major prosecution.

sentences.zh: 四輔臣稱旨，亦謂太祖、太宗時，八旗莊田廬舍，依左右翼順序分給。

translations.literal: The four regents, pleasing the throne, also said that in the eras of Taizu and Taizong, estates, fields, and lodges of the Eight Banners had been allotted according to the order of the left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: The four regents declared, as the throne wished, that under Taizu and Taizong banner estates and lodges had been distributed in wing order.

sentences.zh: 既入關，睿親王多爾衮使鑲黄旗處右翼之末，正白旗圈地本當屬鑲黄旗，今還與相易，亦以復舊制。

translations.literal: After entering the passes Prince Rui Dorgon had placed the Bordered Yellow Banner at the end of the right wing; the Plain White estates ought to belong to the Bordered Yellow, and now they were exchanged back—again to restore the old system.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest Prince Rui had set the Bordered Yellow Banner at the tail of the right wing; Plain White allotments rightly belonged to Bordered Yellow and were now swapped back to restore the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 索尼故不慊蘇克薩哈，顧見鼇拜势日張，與蘇克薩哈不相容，内怵；

translations.literal: Sonin had long been displeased with Suksaha, but seeing Oboi’s power grow daily and that Suksaha could not tolerate him, he was inwardly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Sonin had never been easy with Suksaha, yet as Oboi’s power swelled and Suksaha could not abide him, he grew fearful within;

sentences.zh: 又念年已老，多病，康熙六年三月，遂與蘇克薩哈、遏必隆、鼇拜共爲奏請上親政。

translations.literal: he also thought himself old and often ill—in the third month of Kangxi year six he joined Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi in memorializing that the emperor should take personal rule.
translations.idiomatic: remembering too his age and many illnesses, in the third month of Kangxi six he joined Suksaha, Ebilun, and Oboi in asking the emperor to assume personal rule.

sentences.zh: 上未即允，而詔褒索尼忠，加授一等公，與前授一等伯並世襲，索尼辭，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not at once consent, but an edict praised Sonin’s loyalty, added grant of first-rank duke on top of the earlier first-rank baron, both hereditary—Sonin declined and was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not immediately agree, yet praised Sonin’s loyalty and added a hereditary first-rank duke to his barony; Sonin refused and was overruled.

sentences.zh: 六月，卒，諡文忠，賜祭葬有加禮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died; posthumous title Wenzong, with funeral rites beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month, posthumously titled Wenzong, with funeral honors above the usual.

sentences.zh: 七月，乃下索尼等奏，上親政，以第五子心裕襲一等伯，法保襲一等公。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the memorial of Sonin and the others was finally issued and the emperor took personal rule; the fifth son Xinyu inherited the first-rank baron, Fabao the first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sonin’s memorial was promulgated and the emperor began personal rule; the fifth son Xinyu inherited the baroncy, Fabao the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 長子噶布喇官領侍衛内大臣，孝誠皇后父也，十三年，后崩，推恩所生，授一等公，世襲。

translations.literal: The eldest son Gabula served as commanding guardsman of the inner court and was father of Empress Xiaocheng; in the thirteenth year, after the empress’s death, grace was extended to her natal kin and he was made first-rank duke with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Gabula became commanding inner guardsman and father of Empress Xiaocheng; in year thirteen, when the empress died, her family was ennobled with a hereditary first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 第三子索額圖，自有傳。

translations.literal: The third son Suoetu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Suoetu is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈，納喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Suksaha, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Suksaha belonged to the Nara clan and came from the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父蘇納，葉赫貝勒金台什同族。

translations.literal: His father Suna was of the same lineage as Yehe beile Gintaisi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Suna shared lineage with Yehe beile Gintaisi.

sentences.zh: 太祖初创業，來歸，命尚主爲額駙，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: When Taizu was first founding the enterprise, Suna came over and was ordered to marry an imperial princess as efü and was made niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu’s founding days Suna submitted, was made an imperial son-in-law, and appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 累進梅勒額真。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to meile ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to meile ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰初，從太宗征錦州，貝勒莽古爾泰帥偏師衛塔山餉道，蘇納屯塔山西，明兵來攻，擊破之。

translations.literal: Early in Tiancong he followed the Taizong against Jinzhou; Prince Mangguertai led a detached force to guard the Tashan supply route, and Suna camped west of Tashan, defeated Ming troops when they attacked, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tiancong he followed Taizong against Jinzhou; Prince Mangguertai guarded the Tashan supply line with a flank army, and Suna, camped west of Tashan, repulsed the Ming assault.

sentences.zh: 三年，與固山額真武納格擊察哈爾，入境，降其民二千户。

translations.literal: In the third year, with gusa ejen Wunage, he struck the Chahar; entering their territory they reduced two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he and gusa ejen Wunage invaded the Chahar and brought two thousand households to submission.

sentences.zh: 聞降者將爲变，盡歼其男子，俘婦女八千餘，上責其妄殺。

translations.literal: Hearing the surrendered meant to rebel, they slaughtered all the men and took more than eight thousand women captive; the throne rebuked them for reckless killing.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the surrenderers would revolt, they killed every man and took over eight thousand women; the emperor condemned the massacre.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人有自察哈爾逃入明邊者，命蘇納以百人逐之，所俘獲相當。

translations.literal: When Mongols fled from the Chahar into Ming territory, Suna was ordered to pursue with a hundred men and returned with comparable captives.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols fleeing the Chahar into Ming lands were pursued by Suna with a hundred men, who returned with a fair haul of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 累進三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to third-rank ala captain.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to third-rank ala captain.

sentences.zh: 坐隱匿丁壯，削職。

translations.literal: For concealing able-bodied men he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post for hiding able-bodied subjects.

sentences.zh: 尋授正白旗蒙古固山額真。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Mongol gusa ejen of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Mongol gusa ejen of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 崇德初，從伐明，攻雕鹗、長安諸堡及昌平諸城，五十六戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Early in Chongde he followed campaigns against the Ming, attacking the forts of Diaoyu, Chang’an, and the cities of Changping—fifty-six battles, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In early Chongde he campaigned against the Ming, taking forts at Diaoyu and Chang’an and cities around Changping—fifty-six victories in all.

sentences.zh: 又攻破容城。

translations.literal: He also stormed Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 及出邊，后队潰，坐罰鍰。

translations.literal: On the withdrawal the rear guard collapsed and he was fined.
translations.idiomatic: Marching out, the rear guard broke and he was mulcted.

sentences.zh: 又從伐朝鲜，擊破朝鲜軍，俘其將。

translations.literal: He again followed the invasion of Korea, broke the Korean army, and captured their general.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Korean expedition, routed the Korean forces, and took their general prisoner.

sentences.zh: 以朝鲜王出谒時亂班釋甲，又自他道還，坐罰鍰。

translations.literal: When the Korean king came out to pay homage he disturbed the ranks and doffed armor; returning by another route, he was fined again.
translations.idiomatic: At the king’s audience he threw the ranks into disorder and laid aside armor; leaving by another road, he was fined once more.

sentences.zh: 尋以讞獄有所徇，坐罷，仍專管牛錄事。

translations.literal: Soon, for partiality in a judicial case, he was dismissed but still managed niru affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for favoritism in a legal case, he was removed yet kept sole charge of niru business.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shunzhi year five.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈初授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Suksaha was first made niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Suksaha began as niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗圍錦州，明總督洪承疇師赴援，太宗親帥大軍蹙之，蘇克薩哈戰有功，授牛錄章京世職，晉三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in besieging Jinzhou; when Ming Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou came to relieve the city the Taizong led the main army to press him—Suksaha fought with merit, was granted hereditary niru captain, and advanced to third-rank ala captain.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde six he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang at Jinzhou; when Hong Chengchou marched to relieve it Taizong pressed him with the main host—Suksaha distinguished himself, received a hereditary niru captaincy, and rose to third-rank ala captain.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，世祖命追復蘇納世職，以蘇克薩哈並襲爲三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi the Shizu Emperor ordered Suna’s hereditary office restored and Suksaha to inherit jointly as third-rank ashan ihaan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi seven the emperor restored Suna’s hereditary rank and had Suksaha inherit jointly as third-rank ashan ihaan.

sentences.zh: 尋授議政大臣，進一等，加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Soon he was made deliberating minister, advanced to first rank, with added tosaha banner rank.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became deliberating minister, rose to first rank, and gained an added tosaha banner.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈隸睿親王多爾衮屬下，王薨，蘇克薩哈與王府護衛詹岱等訐王謀移駐永平諸逆狀，及殡斂服色違制，王坐是追黜。

translations.literal: Suksaha had been under Prince Rui Dorgon; when the prince died, Suksaha with the princely guardsman Zhandai denounced the prince’s plot to move the court to Yongping and other treasonous acts, and violations at the funeral and mourning dress—the prince was posthumously disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: Suksaha had served Prince Rui; after the prince’s death he and guardsman Zhandai exposed plots to shift the court to Yongping and breaches of mourning ritual, bringing posthumous disgrace on the prince.

sentences.zh: 是年，擢巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: That year he was raised to Baturu banner captain.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became Baturu banner captain.

sentences.zh: 十年，孫可望寇湖廣，命蘇克薩哈偕固山額真陳泰率禁旅出鎮湖南，與经略洪承疇會剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Sun Kewang raided Huguang; Suksaha was ordered with gusa ejen Chen Tai to lead the forbidden troops to garrison Hunan and join Commissioner-General Hong Chengchou in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Sun Kewang harried Huguang; Suksaha and gusa ejen Chen Tai led the guards army to Hunan to join Hong Chengchou’s campaign.

sentences.zh: 十二年，劉文秀遣其將盧明臣等分兵犯岳州、武昌，蘇克薩哈邀擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Liu Wenxiu sent generals Lu Mingchen and others to attack Yuezhou and Wuchang; Suksaha intercepted and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Liu Wenxiu’s generals Lu Mingchen and others struck Yuezhou and Wuchang; Suksaha met and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 文秀引兵寇常德，戰舰蔽江，蘇克薩哈六戰皆捷，縱火焚其舟，斬獲甚眾，明臣赴水死，文秀走貴州。

translations.literal: Wenxiu himself led troops against Changde; war vessels covered the river—Suksaha won six battles, set fire to the fleet, slew and captured in great numbers; Mingchen drowned and Wenxiu fled to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu then assailed Changde with ships crowding the river; Suksaha won six fights, burned the fleet, took heavy toll—Mingchen drowned and Wenxiu fled to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 叙功，晉二等精奇尼哈番，擢領侍衛内大臣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to second-rank jinggin ihaan, made commanding inner guardsman, and given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he rose to second-rank jinggin ihaan, became commanding inner guardsman, and received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 聖祖立，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: When the Sage Emperor ascended the throne he received the testament to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne he was named in the regency.

sentences.zh: 時索尼爲四朝舊臣，遏必隆、鼇拜皆以公爵先蘇克薩哈爲内大臣，鼇拜尤功多，意气凌轹，人多惮之。

translations.literal: Sonin was an old minister of four reigns; Ebilun and Oboi had both been inner ministers as dukes before Suksaha; Oboi especially had many battle honors and overbearing spirit—most men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin was a veteran of four reigns; Ebilun and Oboi had preceded Suksaha as ducal inner ministers, and Oboi’s victories made him overbearing—few dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈以額駙子入侍禁廷，承恩眷，班行亚索尼；

translations.literal: Suksaha, as an imperial son-in-law serving in the forbidden court, enjoyed favor and ranked just below Sonin;
translations.idiomatic: As an imperial son-in-law in the inner court Suksaha enjoyed special favor and stood only beneath Sonin;

sentences.zh: 與鼇拜有姻連，而論事輙龃齬，浸以成隙。

translations.literal: he was related to Oboi by marriage, yet they clashed in council and the rift deepened.
translations.idiomatic: he was kin to Oboi by marriage, yet they quarreled in council until enmity grew.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜隸鑲黄旗，與正白旗互易莊地，遂兴大獄。

translations.literal: Oboi belonged to the Bordered Yellow Banner; the exchange of estates with the Plain White Banner then stirred a great case.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi held the Bordered Yellow Banner; swapping estates with Plain White now ignited a major trial.

sentences.zh: 大學士兼户部尚書蘇納海，總督朱昌祚、巡撫王登聯坐纷更阻挠，下刑部議罪，以律無正条，請鞭責籍沒。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and acting Minister of Revenue Sunahai, Governor-General Zhu Changzuo, and Governor Wang Denglian were judged for obstructing the redistribution; the Board of Punishments found no exact statute and asked flogging and confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sunahai, Governor-General Zhu Changzuo, and Governor Wang Denglian were charged with blocking the land swap; the Board of Punishments, finding no exact article, proposed flogging and confiscation.

sentences.zh: 上览奏，召輔臣議，鼇拜請置重典，索尼、遏必隆不能争，獨蘇克薩哈不对，上因不允。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and summoned the regents; Oboi asked the heavy penalty, Sonin and Ebilun could not object, and Suksaha alone would not speak—the emperor therefore did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed the report and called the regents; Oboi urged death, Sonin and Ebilun could not dissent, Suksaha alone kept silent, and the emperor withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜卒矫命，悉棄市。

translations.literal: Oboi ultimately forged an order and had them all executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi forged a command and had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜以蘇克薩哈與相抗，憾滋甚。

translations.literal: Oboi, because Suksaha resisted him, hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Because Suksaha had opposed him, Oboi’s hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜日益驕恣，蘇克薩哈居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Oboi grew daily more arrogant; Suksaha was often discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi grew ever more overbearing while Suksaha brooded in discontent.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，上親政，加恩輔臣。

translations.literal: In Kangxi year six the emperor took personal rule and showed grace to the regents.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi six the emperor assumed personal rule and rewarded the regents.

sentences.zh: 越日，蘇克薩哈奏乞守先帝陵寝，庶得保全餘生。

translations.literal: The next day Suksaha memorialized asking to guard the late emperor’s tomb and so preserve what life remained.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Suksaha asked leave to guard the late emperor’s mausoleum and live out his days in peace.

sentences.zh: 有旨詰問，鼇拜與其黨大學士班布爾善等遂誣以怨望，不欲歸政，構罪狀二十四款，以大逆論，與其長子内大臣查克旦皆磔死；

translations.literal: An edict questioned him; Oboi with his faction, Grand Secretary Banbursan and others, then slandered him for resentment and unwillingness to yield power, fabricating twenty-four counts of guilt and sentencing great treason—he and his eldest son, inner minister Chakdan, were executed by slow slicing;
translations.idiomatic: Questioned by edict, Oboi and Grand Secretary Banbursan fabricated twenty-four charges of treason and disloyalty—Suksaha and his eldest son Chakdan died by lingchi;

sentences.zh: 餘子六人、孫一人、兄弟子二人皆處斬，籍沒；

translations.literal: six other sons, one grandson, and two brothers’ sons were beheaded and their property confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: six sons, one grandson, and two nephews were beheaded and their estates seized;

sentences.zh: 族人前鋒統領白爾赫圖、侍衛額爾德皆斬：獄上，上不允。

translations.literal: kinsmen the vanguard commander Baierhetu and guardsman Erde were also condemned to death: when the case reached the throne the emperor would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: kinsmen vanguard commander Baierhetu and guardsman Erde were likewise sentenced; the emperor refused approval.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜攘臂上前，强奏累日，卒坐蘇克薩哈處絞，餘悉如議。

translations.literal: Oboi thrust himself forward, forced the memorial for days, and in the end Suksaha was strangled while the rest of the sentence stood.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi stormed forward, pressed the verdict for days, and finally Suksaha was strangled while the rest stood.

sentences.zh: 八年，鼇拜敗，詔以蘇克薩哈虽有罪，不至誅灭子孫，此皆鼇拜挾仇所致，命復官及世爵，以其幼子蘇常壽襲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Oboi fell, an edict said that though Suksaha had guilt he did not deserve extinction of his line—this was all Oboi’s vendetta—and ordered his offices and hereditary titles restored, his young son Suchangshou inheriting.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, after Oboi’s fall, the court held Suksaha’s crime did not warrant annihilation of his house—Oboi’s spite—and restored rank to his son Suchangshou.

sentences.zh: 蘇納海，他塔喇氏，滿州正白旗人。

translations.literal: Sunahai, of the Tatara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sunahai of the Tatara clan came from the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 由王府護衛擢弘文院學士，累遷工部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: From princely guardsman he was raised to academician of the Hongwen Court, advanced to Minister of Works, and given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from princely guardsman to Hongwen academician, then Minister of Works with Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，拜國史院大學士，兼管户部。

translations.literal: When the Sage Emperor ascended the throne he was made Grand Secretary of the Historiography Court and concurrently supervised the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kangxi enthronement he became Grand Secretary of the Historiography Court and oversaw the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時鼇拜擅权，以蘇納海不阿附，嗛之。

translations.literal: Oboi then held power and resented Sunahai for not joining him.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi, holding power, resented Sunahai’s refusal to side with him.

sentences.zh: 尋鼇拜欲以薊、遵化、遷安正白旗諸屯莊改撥鑲黄旗，而别圈民地益正白旗，使旗人诉請牒户部。

translations.literal: Oboi wished to transfer Plain White estates at Ji, Zunhua, and Qian’an to the Bordered Yellow Banner and allot other civilian lands to Plain White; bannermen petitioned the Board of Revenue with documents.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi sought to move Plain White estates in Ji, Zunhua, and Qian’an to Bordered Yellow and compensate with fresh civilian allotments; bannermen flooded the Board of Revenue with petitions.

sentences.zh: 蘇納海持不可，謂旗人安業已久，且奉旨不許再圈民地，宜罷議，鼇拜益衔之，矫旨遣貝子温齊等履勘。

translations.literal: Sunahai objected, saying the bannermen had long settled their livelihoods and an edict forbade further appropriation of civilian land—the matter should stop; Oboi hated him more and forged an order sending Prince Wenqi and others to survey.
translations.idiomatic: Sunahai refused, citing long settlement and an edict against further seizure of civilian soil; Oboi forged orders for Prince Wenqi to survey.

sentences.zh: 旋以鑲黄地不堪耕种疏聞，遂遣蘇納海會直隸總督朱昌祚、巡撫王登聯董理其事。

translations.literal: When Bordered Yellow lands proved unfit for farming he reported it, then sent Sunahai with Zhili Governor-General Zhu Changzuo and Governor Wang Denglian to manage the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Bordered Yellow allotments poor, he dispatched Sunahai with Zhu Changzuo and Wang Denglian to oversee the exchange.

sentences.zh: 昌祚、登聯交章請停圈换，蘇納海亦言屯地难丈量，候明詔進止，鼇拜遂坐以藐视上命，並棄市。

translations.literal: Changzuo and Denglian jointly memorialized to halt the appropriation; Sunahai also said the estates were hard to measure and awaited clear orders—Oboi then condemned them for defying the throne and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo and Denglian begged to stop the swap; Sunahai said the fields could not be measured pending imperial word—Oboi charged contempt and had all three killed.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜獲罪，昭雪復官，諡蘇納海襄愍，昌祚勤愍，登聯悫愍。

translations.literal: When Oboi was punished, they were posthumously cleared—Sunahai titled Xiangmin, Changzuo Qinmin, Denglian Kemin.
translations.idiomatic: After Oboi’s fall they were exonerated—Sunahai as Xiangmin, Changzuo Qinmin, Denglian Kemin.

sentences.zh: 昌祚，字雲門，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Changzuo, style Yunmen, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo, styled Yunmen, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治初，官宗人府啟心郎。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi he served as Qixinlang in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi he was Qixinlang in the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以工部侍郎巡撫浙江，清廉沉毅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, as Vice Minister of Works, he became governor of Zhejiang—incorrupt, steady, and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen, as Vice Minister of Works, he governed Zhejiang with integrity and firmness.

sentences.zh: 平寇盜，撥荒地，給瀕海内徙居民开墾，免其所棄田畝丁糧，戒所司藉端苛斂，浙人德之。

translations.literal: He pacified bandits, allocated wasteland, gave coastal refugees land to open, exempted abandoned fields from corvée and grain levies, and warned officials against pretexts for harsh exaction—the people of Zhejiang were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed brigands, opened wasteland for refugees, exempted abandoned plots from tax and labor, and forbade harsh levies—the Zhejiang people blessed him.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，擢直隸、山東、河南三省總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he was made governor-general of Zhili, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi four he became governor-general of Zhili, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 圈地議起，旗民失業者數十萬人。

translations.literal: When the land appropriation arose, hundreds of thousands of bannermen lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The land swap left hundreds of thousands of banner families destitute.

sentences.zh: 昌祚抗疏力言其不便，卒以冤死。

translations.literal: Changzuo resisted with forceful memorials on the harm, and in the end died wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo protested in strong memorials and died a wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 祀直隸、浙江名宦。

translations.literal: He is enshrined in the temples of eminent officials of Zhili and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to him stand among the worthies of Zhili and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 登聯，字捷軒，漢軍鑲红旗人。

translations.literal: Denglian, style Jiexuan, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Denglian, styled Jiexuan, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 自貢生授河南鄭州知州，薦擢山東濟甯道，累遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: From tribute student he became magistrate of Zhengzhou in Henan, was recommended to Jining circuit in Shandong, and rose to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as tribute student and Zhengzhou magistrate, he rose through Jining circuit to president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，授保定巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he was made governor of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi seventeen he became governor of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 嚴緝捕，盜賊屏息。

translations.literal: He tightened arrest of criminals and bandits vanished.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened pursuit of criminals until banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，以京東諸路圈地擾民，疏請停止，言甚痛切。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi, as lands in the eastern capital region were seized and the people harassed, he memorialized urgently to stop it, his words piercing.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi five, with eastern capital lands seized and people harried, he memorialized passionately to halt it.

sentences.zh: 民聞其死，甚哀之。

translations.literal: When the people heard of his death they grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The people mourned deeply when he died.

sentences.zh: 祀直隸名宦。

translations.literal: He is enshrined among Zhili’s eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He has a place among Zhili’s worthies.

sentences.zh: 白爾赫圖，初由噶布什賢壯達授兵部副理事官。

translations.literal: Baierhetu, first made vice director in the Board of War from a gabushan xianda.
translations.idiomatic: Baierhetu began as vice director of the Board of War from gabushan xianda rank.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，屢從征有功，擢噶布什賢章京。

translations.literal: Through Chongde he followed many campaigns with merit and was raised to gabushan captain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongde he fought repeatedly with distinction and became gabushan captain.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，入關，擊李自成，敗賊將唐通於一片石，多斬獲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, entering the passes, he struck Li Zicheng and at Yipianshi defeated the rebel general Tang Tong with many kills.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi one he entered China, fought Li Zicheng, and at Yipianshi routed Tang Tong with heavy slaughter.

sentences.zh: 尋從豫親王多鐸西剿流寇，克潼關。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Prince Yu Dodo west to suppress the roving bandits and took Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Prince Yu Dodo west, seized Tong Pass, and crushed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 移師江南，徇蘇州，略定浙江、福建。

translations.literal: Moving to the south he took Suzhou and pacified Zhejiang and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the south he took Suzhou and pacified Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 五年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗征湖南，大破賊於湘潭，平宝庆、武冈。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang to Hunan, routed the rebels at Xiangtan, and pacified Shaoyang and Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, with Prince Zheng in Hunan, he smashed rebels at Xiangtan and pacified Shaoyang and Wugang.

sentences.zh: 累功，晉一等阿達哈哈番，擢噶布什賢噶喇依昂邦。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was advanced to first-rank adaha banner and raised to gabushan gala angbang.
translations.idiomatic: For cumulative merit he rose to first-rank adaha banner and gabushan gala angbang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從信郡王多尼征貴州，屢陷陣，進克雲南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Xin Duoni to Guizhou, fought through many battles, and advanced into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he followed Prince Xin Duoni to Guizhou, fought through repeated battles, and entered Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，率兵取永昌府，渡潞江，敗李定國，遂克腾越州。

translations.literal: The next year he led troops to take Yongchang prefecture, crossed the Lu River, defeated Li Dingguo, and took Tengyue prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he took Yongchang, crossed the Lu River, defeated Li Dingguo, and captured Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 明桂王由榔及定國、白文选俱遁入缅甸。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui Youlang with Dingguo and Bai Wenxuan all fled into Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Prince of Gui Youlang, Dingguo, and Bai Wenxuan fled into Burma.

sentences.zh: 信郡王班師，白爾赫圖留駐雲南。

translations.literal: When Prince Xin withdrew his army Baierhetu remained garrisoned in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin withdrew, but Baierhetu stayed to garrison Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 定國入犯，約降將高應凤内應，以由榔印劄诱元江土司那嵩叛，白爾赫圖往剿，斬應凤於陣，那嵩自焚死，賜白金、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Dingguo invaded; the surrendered general Gao Yingfeng plotted treason within, and with Youlang’s sealed letter tempted the Yuanjiang chieftain Na Song to rebel—Baierhetu marched against them, slew Yingfeng in battle, and Na Song burned himself; he was given silver and saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo invaded with turncoat Gao Yingfeng and Yuanjiang chief Na Song, lured by Youlang’s seal; Baierhetu crushed them, slew Yingfeng, and Na Song burned himself—rewarded with silver, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與定西將軍爱星阿會師木邦，缅人献由榔至軍中。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he joined the Dingxi general Ai Xing’a at Mu Bang; the Burmese delivered Youlang to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he joined General Ai Xing’a at Mu Bang; Burma handed over Youlang.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，詔班師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi one the army was ordered home.

sentences.zh: 進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: He was advanced to first-rank ashan ihaan.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to first-rank ashan ihaan.

sentences.zh: 后蘇克薩哈爲鼇拜構陷，以白爾赫圖爲其族弟，竟被禍。

translations.literal: Later, when Suksaha was framed by Oboi, Baierhetu as his cousin was swept into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Oboi framed Suksaha, Baierhetu as kinsman was destroyed with him.

sentences.zh: 八年，上以白爾赫圖無罪枉坐，追復故官世職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor said Baierhetu had been wrongfully condemned and restored his offices and hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight the emperor cleared Baierhetu and restored office and inheritance.

sentences.zh: 尋其子一等侍衛羅鐸訟其父雲南戰功爲鼇拜所抑，未予優叙，詔晉三等精奇尼哈番，賜祭葬，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: Soon his son, first-class guardsman Luoduo, sued that his father’s Yunnan honors had been suppressed by Oboi without due reward—an edict advanced him to third-rank jinggin ihaan, with funeral rites and posthumous title Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoduo then proved Oboi had denied Yunnan honors; the court raised him to third-rank jinggin ihaan with funeral rites and posthumous title Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 遏必隆，钮祜禄氏，滿州鑲黄旗人。

translations.literal: Ebilun, of the Niuhuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ebilun of the Niuhuru clan came from the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 額亦都第十六子，母和碩公主。

translations.literal: The sixteenth son of Eiyedu; his mother was a princess by imperial grant.
translations.idiomatic: He was Eiyedu’s sixteenth son, born to an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，襲一等昂邦章京，授侍衛，管牛錄事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he inherited first-rank angbang captain, was made guardsman, and managed niru affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong eight he inherited first-rank angbang captain, entered the guard, and ran niru business.

sentences.zh: 貝勒尼堪福晉，遏必隆兄圖爾格女也，無子，诈取仆婦女爲己生。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Nikan was daughter of Ebilun’s elder brother Turgai; childless, she falsely took a servant woman’s child as her own.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Nikan’s consort was Turgai’s daughter; having no son, she passed off a servant’s child as hers.

sentences.zh: 事發，遏必隆坐徇庇，奪世職。

translations.literal: When the affair came out Ebilun was punished for shielding her and lost his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Exposed, Ebilun was condemned for complicity and stripped of his inheritance.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，從太宗伐明，營松山，筑長圍守之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde he followed the Taizong against the Ming, camped at Songshan, and built a long encirclement to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde six he followed Taizong against the Ming, investing Songshan behind a long siege line.

sentences.zh: 明總兵曹变蛟率步骑突圍，迭敗之。

translations.literal: Ming commander Cao Bianjiao led infantry and cavalry in a breakout; they were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ming general Cao Bianjiao broke out with horse and foot and was beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 夜三鼓，变蛟集潰卒突犯御營，遏必隆與内大臣錫翰等力戰，殪十餘人，变蛟負创走。

translations.literal: At the third watch of the night Bianjiao gathered routed troops and struck at the imperial camp; Ebilun with inner minister Xi Han and others fought hard, killed more than ten, and Bianjiao fled wounded.
translations.idiomatic: At the third night-watch Bianjiao rallied broken men and rushed the imperial camp; Ebilun and Xi Han slew a dozen before he fled wounded.

sentences.zh: 論功，得優賚。

translations.literal: For merit he received exceptional rewards.
translations.idiomatic: For this deed he won special rewards.

sentences.zh: 七年，從饒餘貝勒阿巴泰等入長城，克薊州；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince Raoyu Abatai and others through the Great Wall and took Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he marched through the Wall with Prince Raoyu Abatai and took Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 進兵山東，攻夏津，先登，拔之：予牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: advancing into Shandong he attacked Xiajin, was first to scale the wall, and captured it—granted hereditary niru captain.
translations.idiomatic: then in Shandong stormed Xiajin first over the wall and received a hereditary niru captaincy.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從順承郡王勒克德浑剿李自成兄子錦於武昌，拔铁門關，進二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Shuncheng Lekdehun to suppress Li Zicheng’s nephew Jin at Wuchang, took Tiemen Pass, and was advanced to second-rank ala captain.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi two, with Prince Shuncheng, he crushed Li Jin at Wuchang, took Tiemen Pass, and rose to second-rank ala captain.

sentences.zh: 五年，兄子侍衛科普索訐其與白旗諸王有隙，设兵護門，奪世職及佐領。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his nephew guardsman Kebusuo denounced him for estrangement from princes of the White Banner, setting troops to guard his gate; he lost hereditary office and assistant command.
translations.idiomatic: In year five nephew Kebusuo accused him of feuding with White Banner princes and guarding his gate with soldiers; he lost rank and command.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，遏必隆訟冤，詔復職。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took personal rule Ebilun pleaded injustice and an edict restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor’s personal rule Ebilun appealed and was restored.

sentences.zh: 科普索旋獲罪，以所襲圖爾格二等公爵令遏必隆並襲爲一等公。

translations.literal: Kebusuo soon fell into guilt; the second-rank duke Turgai had held was ordered inherited jointly by Ebilun as first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: Kebusuo was soon punished; Turgai’s second-rank dukedom was merged into Ebilun’s first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 尋授議政大臣，擢領侍衛内大臣，累加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was made deliberating minister, raised to commanding inner guardsman, and repeatedly given Junior Tutor and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became deliberating minister, commanding inner guardsman, Junior Tutor, and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，受遺詔爲輔政大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he received the testament as regent minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he was named regent by the late emperor’s will.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，聖祖親政，加恩輔臣，特封一等公，以前所襲公爵授長子法喀，賜双眼花翎，加太師。

translations.literal: In Kangxi year six, when the Sage Emperor took personal rule, grace was shown the regents; Ebilun was specially made first-rank duke, the duke he had earlier inherited given to eldest son Faka, granted double-eyed peacock feather, and made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi six the emperor ruled in person, ennobled Ebilun as first-rank duke, gave his prior dukedom to Faka, bestowed double-eyed peacock plumes, and named him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 屢乞罷輔政，許之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged to leave the regency and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged repeatedly to quit the regency and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 四大臣當國，鼇拜獨專恣，屢矫旨誅戮大臣。

translations.literal: While the four great ministers held the state Oboi alone was arbitrary, repeatedly forging edicts to execute ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the four regents Oboi alone ruled by force, forging edicts to kill ministers.

sentences.zh: 遏必隆知其惡，缄默不加阻，亦不劾奏。

translations.literal: Ebilun knew his wickedness yet kept silent without blocking him and did not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Ebilun knew Oboi’s crimes yet neither stopped nor denounced him.

sentences.zh: 八年，上逮治鼇拜，並下遏必隆獄。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor arrested Oboi and also imprisoned Ebilun.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight the emperor seized Oboi and cast Ebilun into prison.

sentences.zh: 康親王傑書讞上遏必隆罪十二，論死，上宥之，削太師，奪爵。

translations.literal: Prince Kang Jieshu reported twelve counts against Ebilun warranting death; the emperor pardoned him, stripped Grand Tutor and title.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Jieshu found twelve capital charges; the emperor spared his life but took Grand Tutor and rank.

sentences.zh: 九年，上念其爲顧命大臣，且勋臣子，命仍以公爵宿衛内廷。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, remembering him as a testament minister and son of a meritorious house, he was ordered to remain duke on guard within the court.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, as testament minister and merit’s son, he kept ducal rank on inner guard duty.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疾笃，车驾親临慰問。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, gravely ill, the imperial carriage came in person to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve, dying, he was visited by the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 及卒，賜祭葬，諡恪僖，御制碑文，勒石墓道。

translations.literal: On his death funeral rites were granted; posthumous title Keyi; the emperor composed an inscription carved on the tomb road.
translations.idiomatic: He died with funeral honors, posthumous title Keyi, and an imperial inscription on his tomb road.

sentences.zh: 十七年，孝昭皇后崩，遏必隆爲后父，降旨推恩所生，敕立家廟，賜御書榜額。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Empress Xiaozhao died, Ebilun as the empress’s father received grace to his natal house, an order to erect a family shrine, and an imperial plaque.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, when Empress Xiaozhao died, Ebilun as her father gained a family shrine and imperial plaque.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，上以遏必隆初襲額亦都世職，命其第四子尹德襲一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year the emperor recalled that Ebilun had first inherited Eiyedu’s hereditary office and ordered fourth son Yinde to inherit first-rank jinggin ihaan.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-one the throne had fourth son Yinde inherit Eiyedu’s first-rank jinggin ihaan.

sentences.zh: 尹德初自佐領授侍衛，從聖祖征噶爾丹，扈跸甯夏。

translations.literal: Yinde first rose from assistant command to guardsman and followed the Sage Emperor against the Dzungars, attending at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Yinde rose from assistant command to guard, followed the emperor against the Dzungars, and attended at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋自都統擢領侍衛内大臣，兼議政大臣。

translations.literal: Soon from commander-in-chief he was raised to commanding inner guardsman and made deliberating minister.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became commander-in-chief, then commanding inner guardsman and deliberating minister.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，以病乞休，許致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, ill, he begged retirement and was permitted to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng five he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，諡悫敬。

translations.literal: Soon he died; posthumous title Minjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, posthumously titled Minjing.

sentences.zh: 尹德恭谨誠朴，宿衛十餘年，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: Yinde was respectful, cautious, and sincere; guarding the throne more than ten years he never faulted.
translations.idiomatic: Yinde was dutiful and plain; for ten years on guard he never erred.

sentences.zh: 兼襲圖爾格二等公，歲禄所入，以均宗族，人皆賢之。

translations.literal: He also inherited Turgai’s second-rank duke; yearly income he shared equally among his clan—all praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing Turgai’s second-rank duke’s income equally among kin, men called him worthy.

sentences.zh: 尋祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: Soon he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，詔晉一等公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong an edict advanced him to first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong one he was posthumously raised to first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜，瓜爾佳氏，滿州鑲黄旗人，衛齊第三子。

translations.literal: Oboi, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, third son of Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi of the Guwalgiya clan came from the Bordered Yellow Banner, third son of Weiqi.

sentences.zh: 初以巴牙喇壯達從征，屢有功。

translations.literal: He first followed campaigns as a Baturu xianda and won merit repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Baturu xianda and won repeated battle honors.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，授牛錄章京世職，任甲喇額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was granted hereditary niru captain and made ala ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong eight he received hereditary niru captain and became ala ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，征皮岛，與甲喇額真准塔爲前鋒，渡海搏戰，敵軍披靡，遂克之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde, campaigning against Pidao, he and ala ejen Zhuntai were vanguard, crossed the sea to fight hand to hand, the enemy broke and fled, and the place was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde two, against Pidao, he and Zhuntai led the vanguard across the sea, routed the foe, and took the island.

sentences.zh: 命優叙，進三等梅勒章京，賜號「巴圖魯」。

translations.literal: For exceptional merit he was advanced to third-rank meile captain and given the title "Baturu."
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded with third-rank meile captain and the title "Baturu."

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗圍錦州，明總督洪承疇赴援，鼇拜輙先陷陣，五戰皆捷，明兵大潰，追擊之，擒斬過半。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in besieging Jinzhou; when Ming Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou came to relieve, Oboi always charged first—five battles, all victories—the Ming army broke and fled; in pursuit more than half were captured or slain.
translations.idiomatic: In year six at Jinzhou, when Hong Chengchou relieved, Oboi led five victorious charges, shattered the Ming host, and slew or captured half in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 功最，進一等，擢巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: His merit was greatest; he was advanced to first rank and made Baturu banner captain.
translations.idiomatic: Highest in merit, he rose to first rank and Baturu banner captain.

sentences.zh: 八年，從貝勒阿巴泰等敗明守關將，進薄燕京，略地山東，多斬獲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed Prince Abatai and others, defeated Ming frontier defenders, advanced on Yanjing, and raided Shandong with many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he broke Ming frontier troops, neared Beijing, and raided Shandong with heavy kills.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，敗明總督范志完總兵、吳三桂軍。

translations.literal: On the triumphant return he defeated Ming Governor Fan Zhiguan’s troops and Wu Sangui’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he beat Fan Zhiguan’s army and Wu Sangui’s force.

sentences.zh: 叙功，進三等昂邦章京，賚賜甚厚。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to third-rank angbang captain with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to third-rank angbang captain with rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，随大兵定燕京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the main army to settle Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi one he helped settle Beijing.

sentences.zh: 世祖考諸臣功績，以鼇拜忠勤戮力，進一等。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor reviewed ministers’ merit he found Oboi loyal and diligent and advanced him to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Oboi loyal and advanced him to first rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，從英親王阿濟格征湖廣，至安陆，破流賊李自成。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince Ying Ajige to Huguang, reached Anlu, and broke the roving bandit Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, with Prince Ying, he reached Anlu and broke Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 進征四川，斬張献忠於陣。

translations.literal: Advancing into Sichuan he slew Zhang Xianzhong in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan he killed Zhang Xianzhong in the field.

sentences.zh: 下遵義、夔州、茂州諸郡縣。

translations.literal: He reduced Zunyi, Kuizhou, Maozhou, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zunyi, Kuizhou, Maozhou, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐事，奪世職。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for an offense, he lost his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he forfeited his inheritance for an offense.

sentences.zh: 又以貝子屯齊訐告謀立肅親王，私結盟誓，論死，詔宥之，罰鍰自贖。

translations.literal: Prince Tunqi also denounced him for plotting to enthrone Prince Su and private oath—alliance; death was decreed but pardoned, fined to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tunqi accused him of scheming for Prince Su; sentenced to death, pardoned, he paid a fine.

sentences.zh: 是年，率兵駐防大同，擊叛鎮姜瓖，迭敗之，克孝義。

translations.literal: That year he led troops to garrison Datong, struck the rebel garrison Jiang Xiang, repeatedly defeated him, and took Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: That year at Datong he repeatedly beat rebel Jiang Xiang and took Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 七年，復坐事，降一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again for an offense, he was reduced to first-rank ashan ihaan.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven another offense cut him to first-rank ashan ihaan.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took personal rule he was made deliberating minister.
translations.idiomatic: At personal rule he became deliberating minister.

sentences.zh: 累進二等公，予世襲。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to second-rank duke with hereditary grant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to second-rank duke with hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 擢領侍衛内大臣，累加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was raised to commanding inner guardsman and given Junior Tutor and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became commanding inner guardsman, Junior Tutor, and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，受顧命輔政。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he received the testament to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he was named regent by testament.

sentences.zh: 既受事，與内大臣費揚古有隙，又惡其子侍衛倭赫及侍衛西住、折克圖、覺羅塞爾弼同直御前，不加禮輔臣。
