translations.literal: Once in office he feuded with inner minister Feiyanggu, hated his son guardsman Wohe and guardsmen Xizhu, Zheketu, and Aisin Gioro Saierbi for attending the imperial presence without honoring the regents.
translations.idiomatic: In office he quarreled with Feiyanggu and hated guardsmen Wohe, Xizhu, Zheketu, and Saierbi for slighting regents at court.

sentences.zh: 遂論倭赫等擅乘御馬及取御用弓矢射鹿，並棄市。

translations.literal: He then judged Wohe and others for riding the imperial horse without leave and taking imperial bows and arrows to shoot deer, and had them all executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He charged them with riding the imperial horse and using imperial bows to hunt deer, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 又坐費揚古怨望，亦論死，並殺其子尼侃、薩哈連，籍其家，以與弟都統穆里瑪。

translations.literal: He also judged Feiyanggu for resentment and sentenced him to death, killing sons Nikan and Sahalian, confiscating the household and giving it to his brother commander Murima.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu was condemned for resentment; sons Nikan and Sahalian were killed, the estate given to brother Murima.

sentences.zh: 初入關，八旗皆有分地。

translations.literal: On first entering the passes every banner had allotted lands.
translations.idiomatic: At the conquest every banner held allotted lands.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾衮領鑲黄旗，定分地在雄、大城、新安、河間、任丘、肅甯、容城諸縣。

translations.literal: Prince Rui Dorgon held the Bordered Yellow Banner; his allotments lay in Xiong, Dacheng, Xin’an, Hejian, Renqiu, Suining, Rongcheng, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui’s Bordered Yellow estates lay across Xiong, Dacheng, Hejian, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 至是已二十年，旗、民相安久。

translations.literal: By now twenty years had passed and bannermen and civilians had long lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years bannermen and civilians had lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜以地確，倡議八旗自有定序，鑲黄旗不當處右翼之末，當與正白旗薊、遵化、遷安諸州縣分地相易。

translations.literal: Oboi, because the Bordered Yellow lands were fertile, urged that the Eight Banners had a fixed order and the Bordered Yellow should not stand at the end of the right wing but should exchange with Plain White allotments in Ji, Zunhua, and Qian’an.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi, coveting fertile Bordered Yellow lands, argued banners had fixed order and demanded swap with Plain White estates in Ji, Zunhua, and Qian’an.

sentences.zh: 正白旗地不足，别圈民地補之。

translations.literal: Plain White lands being insufficient, other civilian lands were to be seized to supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Plain White shortfall was to be filled by fresh seizure of civilian land.

sentences.zh: 中外皆言不便。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court all said it was harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike protested the harm.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈爲正白旗人，與相抗尤力。

translations.literal: Suksaha, a Plain White bannerman, resisted most fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Suksaha of Plain White resisted most fiercely.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜怒，悉逮蘇納海等，棄市。

translations.literal: Oboi in rage seized Sunahai and the rest and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi in fury had Sunahai and others killed.

sentences.zh: 事具蘇克薩哈傳。

translations.literal: The affair is given in Suksaha’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: This is told fully in Suksaha’s biography.

sentences.zh: 又追論故户部尚書英俄爾岱當睿親王摄政時阿王意，授分地亂序，並及他專擅諸事，奪世職。

translations.literal: He also pursued the late Minister of Revenue Enggūldai for currying Prince Rui’s favor during the regency, allotting lands out of order, and other usurpations—his hereditary office was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously condemned Enggūldai for flattering Prince Rui and disordering land allotments, stripping his heirs.

sentences.zh: 時有竊其馬者，鼇拜捕斬之，並殺御馬羣牧長。

translations.literal: When someone stole his horse Oboi caught and killed him, and also killed the imperial stud herdsman.
translations.idiomatic: He executed a horse thief and the imperial stud chief who failed to guard the herds.

sentences.zh: 怒蒙古都統俄訥、喇哈達、宜理布於議政時不附己，即令蒙古都統不與會議。

translations.literal: Angry that Mongol commander-in-chief Ene, Lahada, and Yilibu would not side with him in council, he barred the Mongol commander from meetings.
translations.idiomatic: He excluded Mongol commander Ene and others from council for refusing to follow him.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜受顧命，名列遏必隆後，自索尼卒，班行章奏，鼇拜皆首列。

translations.literal: Oboi received the testament listed after Ebilun; after Sonin’s death he headed every memorial and report.
translations.idiomatic: Named regent after Ebilun, after Sonin’s death Oboi led every memorial.

sentences.zh: 日與弟穆里瑪、姪塞本特、訥莫及班布爾善、阿思哈、噶褚哈、瑪爾賽、泰必圖、濟世、吳格塞等黨比營私，凡事即家定議，然後施行。

translations.literal: Daily he joined his brother Murima, nephew Saibent, Neqi, and Banbursan, Asiha, Gachuha, Maersai, Taibitu, Jishi, Wugesai, and others in faction and private gain; affairs were settled at home before execution.
translations.idiomatic: He met daily with Murima, Saibent, Banbursan, and a clique who decided policy at home before court.

sentences.zh: 侍讀熊賜履應詔陳時政得失，鼇拜惡之，請禁言官不得陳奏。

translations.literal: Reader Xiong Cili answered the imperial call on policy gains and losses; Oboi hated it and asked that censors be forbidden to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Reader Xiong Cili’s policy memorial angered him; he sought to silence censors.

sentences.zh: 上親政，加一等公，其子納穆福襲二等公。

translations.literal: When the emperor took personal rule he was given added first-rank duke; his son Namufu inherited second-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: At personal rule he gained an added first-rank duke; son Namufu inherited second-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 世祖配天，加太師，納穆福加太子少師。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor was matched in Heaven worship he was made Grand Tutor and Namufu Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor’s matching rite he became Grand Tutor and Namufu Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜益專恣。

translations.literal: Oboi grew still more arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi grew yet more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 户部滿尚書缺員，欲以命瑪爾賽，上别授瑪希納，鼇拜援順治間故事，户部置滿尚書二，强請除授。

translations.literal: When the Manchu Minister of Revenue post fell vacant he wished to appoint Maersai; the emperor appointed Maxina instead—Oboi cited Shunzhi precedent for two Manchu ministers of Revenue and forced the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted Maersai as Revenue minister; the emperor chose Maxina—Oboi forced a second Manchu minister by old precedent.

sentences.zh: 漢尚書王弘祚領部久，瑪爾賽不得自擅，乃因事齮而去之。

translations.literal: Han Minister Wang Hongzuo had long headed the ministry and Maersai could not monopolize it; Oboi therefore slandered and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Han minister Wang Hongzuo blocked Maersai; Oboi slandered and ousted him.

sentences.zh: 卒，又擅予諡忠敏。

translations.literal: On Maersai’s death he arbitrarily gave posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When Maersai died Oboi gave him posthumous title Zhongmin on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 工部滿尚書缺員，妄稱濟世才能，强請推補。

translations.literal: When the Manchu Works minister fell vacant he falsely praised Jishi’s talent and forced his promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Jishi into the vacant Manchu Works post by false praise.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，上以鼇拜結黨專擅，勿思悛改，下詔數其罪，命議政王等逮治。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi the emperor, because Oboi formed a faction and acted arbitrarily without repentance, issued an edict listing his crimes and ordered the deliberating princes to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi eight the emperor denounced Oboi’s clique and ordered princes to seize him.

sentences.zh: 康親王傑書等會讞，列上鼇拜大罪三十，論大辟，並籍其家，納穆福亦論死，上親鞫俱實，詔謂：「效力年久，不忍加誅，但褫職籍沒。」

translations.literal: Prince Kang Jieshu and others judged thirty great crimes warranting execution and confiscation; Namufu also sentenced to death; the emperor personally tried them and found all true, yet said: "Long service moves me to spare execution—only strip office and confiscate."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang found thirty capital counts against Oboi and Namufu; the emperor confirmed guilt yet spared their lives, stripping rank and property."

sentences.zh: 納穆福亦免死，俱予禁錮。

translations.literal: Namufu also escaped death; both were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Namufu too was spared death; both were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜死禁所，乃釋納穆福。

translations.literal: When Oboi died in confinement Namufu was released.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi died in custody; Namufu was freed.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，上念其舊勞，追賜一等阿思哈尼哈番，以其從孫蘇赫襲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year the emperor, remembering old service, posthumously granted first-rank ashan ihaan to his collateral grandson Suhe.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-two the throne granted first-rank ashan ihaan to grandson Suhe.

sentences.zh: 蘇赫卒，仍以鼇拜孫達福襲。

translations.literal: When Suhe died Oboi’s grandson Dafu still inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Suhe’s death passed the rank to grandson Dafu.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，賜祭葬，復一等公，予世襲，加封號曰超武。

translations.literal: When the Shizong ascended he granted funeral rites, restored first-rank duke with hereditary succession, and added the honorific Chaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng emperor restored first-rank duke with hereditary title Chaowu and funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年，高宗宣諭羣臣，追覈鼇拜功罪，命停襲公爵，仍襲一等男；

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor announced to the ministers a review of Oboi’s merits and faults and ordered the dukedom not inherited, only first-rank baron;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong forty-five the emperor reviewed Oboi’s deeds, ended the dukedom, and left only first-rank baron;

sentences.zh: 並命當時爲鼇拜誣害諸臣有褫奪世職者，各旗察奏，錄其子孫。

translations.literal: and ordered that ministers wrongly harmed by Oboi who lost hereditary offices should be reported banner by banner and their descendants recorded.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered banners to list descendants of those Oboi had wronged.

sentences.zh: 穆里瑪，衛齊第六子。

translations.literal: Murima was the sixth son of Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Murima was Weiqi’s sixth son.

sentences.zh: 衛齊卒，襲世職牛錄章京，授一等侍衛。

translations.literal: When Weiqi died he inherited the hereditary niru captain, was made first-class guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: At Weiqi’s death he inherited niru captain and became first-class guardsman.

sentences.zh: 順治初，遷甲喇額真世職，累進一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi he was moved to hereditary ala ejen, advanced to first-rank adaha banner with added tosaha banner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he rose to hereditary ala ejen and first-rank adaha with tosaha.

sentences.zh: 從征金声桓，克饒州，遂下南昌。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Jin Shenghuan he took Raozhou and then Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Against Jin Shenghuan he took Raozhou and Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢工部尚書，並授本旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was made Minister of Works and Manchu commander-in-chief of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he became Minister of Works and Manchu banner commander.

sentences.zh: 李自成將李來亨等降於明，窜伏鄖、襄山中，出劫掠爲寇。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng’s general Li Laiheng and others had surrendered to the Ming and lurked in the mountains of Yun and Xiang, raiding as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Laiheng, once Li Zicheng’s man, hid in Yun-Xiang hills and raided as brigands.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，授穆里瑪靖西將軍，圖海定西將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi Murima was made Pacifier of the West and Tu Hai Pacifier of the West, leading armies against them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi two Murima and Tu Hai led western campaigns against them.

sentences.zh: 來亨擁眾據茅麓山，穆里瑪督兵攻圍，九戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Laiheng held Maolu Mountain with a great host; Murima directed the siege and won nine battles.
translations.idiomatic: Laiheng held Maolu Mountain; Murima besieged him and won nine fights.

sentences.zh: 來亨等夜襲總督李國英、提督鄭蛟麟營，穆里瑪赴援，大破之，來亨自焚死，餘眾降。

translations.literal: Laiheng and others raided by night the camps of Governor Li Guoying and Regional Commander Zheng Jiaolin; Murima went to the relief, routed them utterly, Laiheng burned himself to death, and the rest surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Laiheng night-assaulted Governors Li Guoying and Zheng Jiaolin; Murima relieved them, crushed the rebels, Laiheng burned himself, and the remnant surrendered.

sentences.zh: 論功，超進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit he was specially advanced to first-rank ashan ihaan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was raised beyond grade to first-rank ashan ihaan.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜得罪，坐死。

translations.literal: When Oboi fell into guilt he was condemned to death for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Oboi was punished Murima died for complicity.

sentences.zh: 班布爾善，太祖諸孫輔國公塔拜子也。

translations.literal: Banbursan was son of Taizu’s grandson, Prince of the State Assisting the Nation Tabai.
translations.idiomatic: Banbursan was son of Auxiliary State Prince Tabai, a grandson of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 初封三等奉國將軍，累進輔國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed third-rank prince of the state assisting the nation and was repeatedly advanced to auxiliary state prince.
translations.idiomatic: He began as third-rank assisting-state prince and rose to auxiliary state prince.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，以領侍衛内大臣拜秘書院大學士，諂事鼇拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, as commanding inner guardsman he was made Grand Secretary of the Secretariat and fawned on Oboi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi six, commanding inner guardsman, he became Grand Secretary and flattered Oboi.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，王大臣劾奏班布爾善大罪二十一，坐絞。

translations.literal: When the affair collapsed deliberating prince Jieshu memorialized twenty-one great crimes of Banbursan and he was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: After Oboi’s fall Prince Jieshu charged him with twenty-one capital crimes and he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 同時坐鼇拜黨罪至死者，吏部尚書阿思哈、侍郎泰必圖、兵部尚書噶褚哈、工部尚書濟世、内秘書院學士吳格塞及鼇拜姪塞本特、訥莫、瑪爾賽，追奪官爵，削諡。

translations.literal: At the same time those who died for Oboi’s faction included Minister of Revenue Asiha, Vice Minister Taibitu, Minister of War Gachuha, Minister of Works Jishi, academician of the Inner Secretariat Wugesai, and Oboi’s nephews Saibent, Neqi, and Maersai—all posthumously stripped of office, titles, and posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: Executed with the faction were Revenue minister Asiha, War minister Gachuha, Works minister Jishi, academician Wugesai, and nephews Saibent, Neqi, and Maersai—all disgraced posthumously.

sentences.zh: 論曰：四輔臣當國時，改世祖之政，必舉太祖、太宗以爲辭。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the four regents held the state they altered the Shizu Emperor’s policies yet always cited Taizu and Taizong as their warrant.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: the four regents changed Shunzhi’s policies yet always invoked Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 然世祖罷明季三餉，四輔臣時復徵練餉，並令併入地丁考成。

translations.literal: Yet the Shizu Emperor had abolished the Ming’s three extractions; under the four regents the practice levy was revived and ordered merged into the land-and-service tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi had ended the Ming’s three surcharges; the regents revived the practice levy and folded it into the land tax.

sentences.zh: 此非太祖、太宗舊制然也，則又將何辭？

translations.literal: This was not the old system of Taizu and Taizong—what excuse remained?
translations.idiomatic: That was no Taizu or Taizong institution—what warrant could they claim?

sentences.zh: 索尼忠於事主，始終一節，錫以美諡，誠無愧焉。

translations.literal: Sonin was loyal to his lord from first to last without change; honored with a fine posthumous title, he truly deserved no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Sonin served loyally to the end and earned his noble posthumous name without reproach.

sentences.zh: 蘇克薩哈見忌同列，遂致覆宗。

translations.literal: Suksaha, envied by his colleagues, was brought to the extinction of his house.
translations.idiomatic: Suksaha, hated by peers, saw his line destroyed.

sentences.zh: 遏必隆黨比求全，幾及於禍。

translations.literal: Ebilun joined factions to save himself and nearly came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Ebilun clung to faction for safety and nearly perished with it.

sentences.zh: 鼇拜多戮無辜，功不掩罪。

translations.literal: Oboi slaughtered many innocents; merit cannot cover his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Oboi killed countless innocents; his battles cannot excuse his guilt.

sentences.zh: 聖祖不加誅殛，亦云幸矣。

translations.literal: That the Sage Emperor did not put him to death may also be called fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: That the Kangxi Emperor spared his life was itself a mercy.
